reconcile.note: Gill reads the refusal in Mark as declining only a sign from heaven, consistent with the many signs already shown and the coming sign of Jonah.

discrepancy.note: Strauss presses the tension between Jesus refusing any sign and the Jonah exception granted in the same breath.

quotes.text: he declares that there shall be no sign given to this generation … that there shall no sign be given to it but the sign of Jonah the prophet
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), §72, on Mark 8:12 and Matthew 12:39.

sides.snippet: no sign will be given to this generation.
sides.verseText: He sighed deeply in his spirit, and said, \"Why does this generation seek a sign? Most assuredly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.\"

sides.snippet: Therefore Jesus did many other signs in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book;
sides.verseText: Therefore Jesus did many other signs in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book;
